title: Not Implemented
statement: Implement `solve(left_type, right_type)`. Both are `point` or `other`. If both are `point`, return `compare`. If the right side is `other`, return `notimplemented` so Python can try the reflected equality. Do not return `false` for a foreign type. Returning false would claim the values are unequal without giving the other class a chance.
constraints: A foreign right-hand side returns notimplemented
hints: Any other combination in these tests returns notimplemented. The interesting case is point versus other.
Do not return the string false.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Returning NotImplemented from __eq__ asks Python to try the other operand's __eq__.

editorial: Returning NotImplemented from __eq__ asks Python to try the other operand's __eq__. Returning False ends the comparison. A point compared to a tuple should not decide the tuple's side of the story. The string notimplemented is that sentinel.
